INT. CLOCK TOWER WORKSHOP - DAWN - CONTINUOUS. A round room full of gears, pendulum weights and hanging tools. Dust turns in the light from a single window.
Cast direction for characters present in this scene; do not add appearances beyond the screenplay:
WREN. Appearance: As the script introduces them: “WREN ALDER, an apprentice clockmaker in a mustard scarf and a leather apron, runs along the harbour wall with a toolbag.”. Age range: not stated in the script. Wardrobe: Everyday clothes that suit the scene..
OSWIN. Appearance: A male character. As the script introduces him: “OSWIN FELL, the old clockmaker, white-haired and stooped, sits at a bench with a magnifying loupe on a cord around his neck.”. Age range: not stated in the script. Wardrobe: Everyday clothes that suit the scene..

Shot direction (creative intent; preserve the screenplay action):
Shot size: wide
Camera angle: eye level
Camera movement intent: static
Performance: Natural and understated
Sound intent: Quiet room tone
Transition intent: Cut on the new location
Key light: Soft window light
Time of day: day
Style bible (one look for the whole feature, the same in every sequence; preserve the screenplay action and the cast direction):
Look: Go soft and painterly: cool silver-grey dawns, amber lamplight in the workshop, deep teal storm night, then a golden sunset finish. Give special treatment to the escape wheel close-ups, the green-lit chapel, the belfry bell swing, and the final rise past the clock face to the sky.
Palette: Natural colour true to each location's light, graded the same way in every sequence.
Lighting: Soft natural daylight outside, soft window light inside, low motivated practical light at night.
Lens and framing: Wide to open each location, medium for action, close-ups for dialogue; eye-level and steady.
Tone: warm and hopeful
Sound: Make it a motif. Use a warm acoustic score of strings, piano, celesta and soft accordion, with the clock's tick as a rhythmic pulse.
